citations.short: Authority lacking to review records, investigate errors
citations.long: The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred.

citations.short: Cleaning/maintenance records not kept
citations.long: Records are not kept for the maintenance, cleaning, and inspection of equipment.

citations.short: Computer control of master formula records
citations.long: Appropriate controls are not exercised over computers or related systems to assure that changes in master production and control records or other records are instituted only by authorized personnel.

citations.short: SOPs not followed / documented
citations.long: Written production and process control procedures are not followed in the execution of production and process control functions.

citations.short: Strict control not exercised over labeling issued
citations.long: Strict control is not exercised over labeling issued for use in drug product labeling operations.

citations.short: Following/documenting laboratory controls
citations.long: Established laboratory control mechanisms are not followed and documented at the time of performance.

citations.short: QC- required operations equipment, instruments, controls
citations.long: Your quality control personnel did not perform required operations for equipment and controls.

citations.short: Procedures not  in writing, fully followed
citations.long: The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit are not in writing.

citations.short: Equipment Design, Size and Location
citations.long: Equipment used in the manufacture, processing, packing or holding of drug products is not of appropriate design, of adequate size, and suitably located to facilitate operations for its intended use.

citations.short: Calibration/Inspection/Checking not done
citations.long: Routine calibration of mechanical equipment is not performed according to a written program designed to assure proper performance.

citations.short: Reports of Analysis (Components)
citations.long: Reports of analysis from component suppliers are accepted in lieu of testing each component for conformity with all appropriate written specifications, without establishing the reliability of the supplier's analyses through appropriate validation of the supplier's test results at appropriate intervals.

citations.short: Scientifically sound laboratory controls
citations.long: Laboratory controls do not include the establishment of scientifically sound and appropriate test procedures designed to assure that in-process materials conform to appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality and purity.

citations.short: Data secured in course of each test
citations.long: Laboratory records do not include a complete record of all data secured in the course of each test, including all graphs, charts, and spectra from laboratory instrumentation, properly identified to show the drug product tested.

citations.short: Procedures to be written and followed
citations.long: Procedures describing the handling of all written and oral complaints regarding a drug product are not established and written.

citations.short: Buildings not maintained in good state of repair
citations.long: Buildings used in the manufacturing, processing, packing, and holding of a drug product are not maintained in a good state of repair.

citations.short: Calibration/Inspection/Checking not done
citations.long: Routine calibration of mechanical equipment is not performed according to a written program designed to assure proper performance.

citations.short: Backup data not assured as exact and complete
citations.long: Backup data is not assured as exact and secure from alteration, erasure or loss through keeping hard copy or alternate systems.

citations.short: Cleaning / Sanitizing / Maintenance
citations.long: Equipment and utensils are not cleaned at appropriate intervals to prevent contamination that would alter the safety, identity, strength, quality or purity of the drug product.

citations.short: Control procedures to monitor and validate performance
citations.long: Control procedures are not established which monitor the output and validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in-process material and the drug product.

citations.short: Scientifically sound laboratory controls
citations.long: Laboratory controls do not include the establishment of scientifically sound and appropriate test procedures designed to assure that in-process materials conform to appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality and purity.

citations.short: Annual visual exams of drug products
citations.long: Reserve samples from representative sample lots or batches of drug products selected by acceptable statistical procedures are not examined visually at least once a year for evidence of deterioration.

citations.short: Items to cover on annual reviews
citations.long: Written procedures are not established for evaluations done at least annually and including provisions for a review of complaints, recalls, returned or salvaged drug products, and investigations conducted for each drug product.
